intentAndPurpose.intent: Toggle button with text label and optional start/end slots for binary selection within groups.

rules.name: high attention
useWhen: selected state needs bold fill emphasis

rules.name: medium attention
useWhen: selected state with subtle tinted fill

rules.name: low attention
useWhen: selected state with ghost appearance and accent border

props.name: attention
props.description: Attention level — determines the visual prominence of the SELECTED state. high → bold fill; medium → subtle fill; low → ghost with accent border. The UNSELECTED state is always muted ghost regardless of attention. Default: 'high'.

props.name: condensed
props.description: Condensed mode: reduces height and horizontal padding while keeping the same typography. Only applies when contained=true.

props.name: contained
props.description: When true (default), renders a pill container with background, border, and padding. When false, renders inline text/icon only — no background, border, or padding. condensed and fullWidth do not apply when contained=false.

props.name: end
props.description: Content to render after the label (icon, etc.)

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to fill container width. Only applies when contained=true.

props.name: loading
props.description: Loading state — disables interaction and shows reduced opacity.

props.name: selected
props.description: Selected state (controlled). Maps to Toggle pressed.

props.name: start
props.description: Content to render before the label (icon, etc.)

interactionBehavior.summary: SelectableButton is a Base UI Toggle, so every click flips `aria-pressed` — and unlike Chip, it starts UNSELECTED (`defaultSelected` defaults to `false`). Attention colours the SELECTED look only; unselected is always a muted ghost regardless of attention. Press feedback is a scale DOWN (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`, 3%; 1% when `fullWidth`) with NO pressed fill token at all. `contained={false}` strips the pill so hover fills never apply and selection is colour-only. `loading` implies disabled: the start/label/end slots go to `opacity: 0` and a centred spinner takes over without the button changing size.
hover: Every hover rule is wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)` and excluded for `[data-contained="false"]` and `[data-disabled]`.
UNSELECTED (contained) tints the transparent rest fill to `--{Role}-Hover`.

SELECTED at `attention="high"` steps the fill to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` (or keeps `--{Role}-Material-Fill` when a metallic gradient is assigned); at `medium` it steps to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; at `low` it ADDS a `--{Role}-Hover` fill over the rest transparent-plus-accent-hairline.
Label and icon colours never change on hover — only the background.
`contained={false}` has no hover fill and no hover colour shift, so an inline selectable is visually inert on hover.
press: The entire button scales DOWN: `scale(1 - tapScale/100)` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default` at 3%, dropping to `--Motion-Tap-Scale-FullWidth` (1%) when `fullWidth`. This is the same direction as Button, opposite to SelectableIconButton / SelectableSingleTextButton which grow.
There is no `:active` fill, border, or text-colour rule — press colour feedback does not exist. The squash is the entire pressed look.
The scale rule is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded and is NOT excluded for `contained={false}`, so an uncontained selectable still squashes on tap even though its colours do not change.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
`:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click selects without painting a halo.
With `contained={false}` the button sets `border-radius: 0` and has no padding, so the halo is a tight square around the text rather than a pill ring.
keyboard: Base UI Toggle renders a native `<button aria-pressed>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both toggle — both paths are covered by tests.
Controlled via `selected` / `onSelectedChange`; uncontrolled via `defaultSelected` (default `false`). Pass `value` when nesting inside a ToggleGroup.
Disabled and loading are natively `disabled`, so they are out of the tab order and cannot toggle.
selected: Selected maps to Base UI Toggle's `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and matched in CSS with `[data-pressed]`.
It defaults to FALSE in uncontrolled mode — a bare `<SelectableButton>Like</SelectableButton>` renders unselected. This is the opposite of Chip, which defaults to selected.

`attention` colours the SELECTED contained look only: high → `--{Role}-Bold` fill with `--{Role}-Bold-High` text and a transparent border; medium → `--{Role}-Subtle` fill with `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text; low → transparent fill with a `--{Role}-Bold` hairline and accent text. Unselected is always transparent + `--{Role}-Medium-Text` + `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline, ignoring attention.

`contained={false}` never paints a pill: unselected high uses `--{Role}-High` text, unselected medium/low use `--{Role}-Medium-Text`; selected high uses `--{Role}-TintedA11y`, selected medium/low use `--{Role}-High`.
Start/end slot icons inherit `currentColor` and, when selected contained high, are remapped onto `--{Role}-Bold-High` so they stay readable on the bold fill.
loading: `loading` implies disabled — `isDisabled = disabled || loading` — so the native `disabled` attribute is set and `onSelectedChange` stops firing.
`aria-busy="true"` and `data-loading` are set; the `.loading` class is applied.
The start slot, label, and end slot go to `opacity: 0` rather than `display: none`, which keeps their boxes in layout — the button does not resize — and keeps the label in the accessibility tree.
The spinner is absolutely positioned across the button's box, so it lands centred over the hidden content.
disabled: `disabled` (and loading) emit Base UI's `data-disabled`, which dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`.

Because the underlying button is natively `disabled` AND has `pointer-events: none`, the `not-allowed` cursor is not observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. Known, accepted system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
Every hover fill and the tap-scale are qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`. Disabling does not clear the selected styling — it only dims whatever selected/unselected look was showing.
touch: Hover fills never apply on touch-only devices; the 3% (or 1% full-width) squash is the entire visual response to a tap, because there is no pressed fill.
The whole pill is the hit target — start, label, and end sit inside the toggle button.
